source: Sample of 271 letters (10 items) and 164 emails (11 items) spanning Jan 2025 council meetings and simulated 2026 agenda items; taxonomy derived from the text of those comments.
stance_definition: support = commenter favors the proposal, action, or appointment being discussed; oppose = commenter is against it or asks the council to vote no; neutral = commenter is mixed, undecided, or raises a question without taking a side; unclear = content-free cover note, forwarded attachment notice, or message too vague to place on the item.

categories.label: Housing & Affordability Policy
categories.description: Comments about housing supply, zoning, rent regulation, affordable housing financing, and displacement. The main ask is a policy change that affects how much housing exists or what it costs.
include: Zoning changes (upzoning, fourplex reform, ADU permits) aimed at increasing or restricting housing
Rent ordinance caps, eviction protections, and landlord-tenant policy
Affordable housing bond issuers, tax-exempt financing, and housing development approvals
Comments about being priced out, rent increases, or housing supply shortage
exclude: Habitability complaints (no hot water, mold) → code_enforcement_habitability
Permitting process delays not tied to housing supply policy → code_enforcement_habitability
Rezoning for non-residential uses (retail strip mall) → environment_development_review
examples: I strongly SUPPORT legalizing fourplexes citywide. We have a housing shortage and single-family-only zoning is a big reason.

I am writing to support the staff recommendation as well as the memo from Mayor Mahan, and Councilmembers Kamei, Foley and Cohen. The memo recommends allowing any affordable housing developer to use any bond issuer approved by the State of California.
I strongly SUPPORT lowering the annual rent cap under the Apartment Rent Ordinance. Working people are being priced out of the city we grew up in.

subcategories.label: Zoning & Density Reform
subcategories.description: Comments supporting or opposing citywide upzoning, fourplex legalization, ADU policy, and other land-use rule changes meant to increase or restrict overall housing supply.

subcategories.label: Rent Stabilization & Caps
subcategories.description: Comments about the Apartment Rent Ordinance, annual rent-increase caps, and rent-control policy, including both tenant support and landlord opposition.

subcategories.label: Tenant Protections & Eviction
subcategories.description: Comments focused on eviction defenses, anti-retaliation protections, loophole-closing in the rent ordinance, and safeguards for renters facing displacement.

subcategories.label: Affordable Housing Financing
subcategories.description: Comments about tax-exempt bond issuers, multifamily revenue bond policy, and the mechanics of financing deed-restricted affordable housing development.

subcategories.label: Housing Supply & Infrastructure Readiness
subcategories.description: Comments linking new housing supply to concerns about whether supporting infrastructure—sewers, water, schools—can handle increased density.

categories.label: Public Safety & Emergency Response
categories.description: Comments about policing, non-sworn response programs, 911 alternatives, crime prevention, surveillance, and public-safety budget priorities. The main ask is about who responds to emergencies and how.
include: Support or opposition to alternative or co-response programs for 911 calls
Patrol levels, sworn vs. non-sworn staffing, community service officers
Surveillance cameras, license-plate readers, and privacy trade-offs
Crime prevention: youth programs, lighting as safety investment
Concerns about specific crimes (car break-ins, catalytic converter theft) tied to a policy ask
exclude: Streetlight outages as infrastructure maintenance → infrastructure_streets
Immigrant protection from federal enforcement → governance_civic_rights
examples: I SUPPORT expanding non-sworn community service officers and better lighting/cameras rather than only adding armed police.
We ask members of PSFSS to defer accepting the report and direct staff to return within 60 days with updated recommendations for a disability-inclusive alternative response.
Crime is up and you want to cut sworn officers? I OPPOSE any police budget cut. Fund more patrols now.

subcategories.label: Patrol & Sworn Officer Staffing
subcategories.description: Comments about funding or cutting sworn police officer positions, patrol frequency, and response times to crime incidents.

subcategories.label: Alternative & Co-Response Programs
subcategories.description: Comments on non-sworn or civilian responders for 911 calls, including disability-inclusive alternatives and YWCA/SURJ-type co-response proposals.

subcategories.label: Cameras, Surveillance & Privacy
subcategories.description: Comments weighing the use of city surveillance cameras and license-plate readers against resident privacy rights.

subcategories.label: Crime Prevention & Youth Programs
subcategories.description: Comments supporting late-night youth programs, job training, and lighting as upstream crime-prevention investments rather than enforcement.

categories.label: Streets & Infrastructure
categories.description: Comments about road surfaces, streetlights, sidewalks, storm drains, and other public right-of-way infrastructure. The main ask is repair, maintenance, or funding for physical infrastructure.
include: Pothole and pavement repair requests tied to a funding or policy decision
Streetlight outages and maintenance contracts
Sidewalk drainage, storm drain backups, and flood risk from inadequate infrastructure
Derelict buildings affecting public sidewalks or transit rights-of-way
exclude: Flood risk from a new development project → environment_development_review
Code enforcement on private property → code_enforcement_habitability
Permitting for street work → code_enforcement_habitability
examples: For almost a month now the streetlights along King Road between Story and Tully have been out. The whole stretch is pitch black.
There is a huge pothole on Alma Avenue just west of the Washington area. It is at least two feet across and deep.
Every rain over an inch the storm drain backs up and water reaches the driveways.

subcategories.label: Pothole & Pavement Repair
subcategories.description: Comments reporting specific potholes or crumbling road surfaces and requesting emergency or scheduled repair, including debates about patch quality vs. full repaving.

subcategories.label: Streetlight Outages & Reliability
subcategories.description: Comments about extended streetlight outages, copper-wire theft, contractor reliability, and funding for permanent wiring upgrades on corridors like Story/King.

subcategories.label: Storm Drain & Flooding
subcategories.description: Comments about storm-drain backups, water reaching driveways and garages, and requests for Public Works or Water District intervention.

subcategories.label: Infrastructure Equity & Accountability
subcategories.description: Comments arguing that lower-income or East Side neighborhoods wait longer for repairs than wealthier areas, and requesting equal service standards.

categories.label: Environment & Development Review
categories.description: Comments about environmental review, land-use approvals, rezoning, and the environmental or community impacts of proposed development projects. The main ask concerns whether a specific project should be approved, denied, or revised.
include: EIR certification and environmental impact review for new development
Rezoning applications for specific parcels
Flood risk, water demand, air quality, or habitat concerns raised in the context of a project
Community benefit agreements, traffic impacts, and neighborhood character in response to a development proposal
exclude: Citywide zoning policy (fourplex reform, upzoning) → housing_affordability_policy
Air quality concerns not tied to a specific project → other
Infrastructure failures unrelated to new development → infrastructure_streets
examples: the Terra Verde EIR appears to understate groundwater and cooling-water demand and does not adequately model cumulative flood impacts. I OPPOSE certification of the EIR as written.
I OPPOSE rezoning the parcel near Blossom Hill Road for another strip mall. We have empty retail already and it'll add traffic to a bad intersection.
cooling-water demand, backup generator emissions, cumulative flood impacts, and inadequate community engagement

subcategories.label: EIR & Environmental Review
subcategories.description: Comments on the adequacy of Environmental Impact Reports, including concerns about understated water demand, flood modeling, and cumulative environmental impacts.

subcategories.label: Flood & Water Risk
subcategories.description: Comments specifically about flood risk, groundwater depletion, and water-use concerns raised in relation to a proposed development project.

subcategories.label: Traffic & Neighborhood Character
subcategories.description: Comments opposing a development due to traffic congestion, excess vacant retail, or incompatibility with existing neighborhood character.

subcategories.label: Conditional Approval & Community Benefits
subcategories.description: Comments supporting a project only if specific conditions—water recycling, community benefit agreements, or noise mitigation—are attached to approval.

categories.label: Code Enforcement & Permitting
categories.description: Comments about building code enforcement, property habitability, permit backlogs, and inspection processes. The main ask is that the city enforce standards on existing properties or speed up permitting.
include: Rental unit habitability problems (no hot water, mold, pest) and requests for inspector dispatch
Derelict or blighted buildings and code enforcement response
Permitting delays for ADUs, small businesses, solar, or remodels
Permit fee levels and the code enforcement staffing or operations study session
exclude: Citywide policy on rental inspections is the item → still code_enforcement_habitability if the main ask is about habitability enforcement
Rezoning or EIR for new construction → environment_development_review
Sidewalk or street infrastructure failing near a property → infrastructure_streets
examples: Tenants at Cedar Court Apartments near Tully Road have had NO hot water for nine days. The landlord ignores us. I OPPOSE the slow code enforcement response.
My ADU permit has been 'in review' for EIGHT months. Every cycle they ask for one new thing.
I would like to know what PBCE and DOT staff are empowered to do when a derelict building on private property is endangering safety along public transportation rights-of-way.

subcategories.label: Habitability Failures
subcategories.description: Comments reporting urgent habitability deficiencies—no hot water, mold, broken security—and demanding inspector dispatch and landlord accountability.

subcategories.label: Derelict Buildings & Blight
subcategories.description: Comments about abandoned or blighted buildings that endanger adjacent sidewalks, transit rights-of-way, or neighborhood quality.

subcategories.label: Permit Backlog & Delays
subcategories.description: Comments about prolonged ADU, small-business, solar, or remodel permit reviews and requests to reduce turnaround times or waive fees for delayed projects.

subcategories.label: Permit Fees & Staffing
subcategories.description: Comments opposing fee increases without service improvement and calling for more plan-check staff rather than software-only process reforms.

categories.label: Governance & Civic Rights
categories.description: Comments about local governance decisions, voter rights, tax policy, legislative advocacy, immigrant protections, and council appointments. The main ask concerns how power is exercised or who holds office.
include: Opposition to or support for lowering voter thresholds for taxes (Prop 13, IGR)
Immigrant protection resolutions and sanctuary city policies
Council district appointments and special elections
Legislative program priorities and IGR advocacy positions
Boards and commissions appointments and fairness concerns
exclude: Specific service-delivery concerns about policing → public_safety_emergency_response
Specific project approvals → environment_development_review
examples: I am opposed to lower the voter threshold for approving property taxes and undermining Prop 13. This will be devastating for most of the seniors.

I am writing to express my strong support for the memo proposed by Councilmembers Ortiz, Campos, Cohen, and Candelas, which outlines critical actions to protect our city's residents from the harmful policies of the incoming presidential administration.
I am writing to urge you to appoint Jahmal Williams to be the Interim Councilmember for District 3.

subcategories.label: Voter Threshold & Prop 13
subcategories.description: Comments opposing or supporting IGR advocacy to lower the supermajority threshold for property taxes, referencing Proposition 13 and the defeat of Proposition 5.

subcategories.label: Immigrant Protection & Sanctuary Policy
subcategories.description: Comments supporting or opposing the city resolution affirming protections for immigrant residents, limiting police collaboration with federal immigration enforcement.

subcategories.label: Council Appointments & Special Elections
subcategories.description: Comments nominating or endorsing candidates for interim council appointments, including letters of support for District 3 candidates.

subcategories.label: Boards, Commissions & Appointments Fairness
subcategories.description: Comments questioning who is appointed to city boards and commissions and whether the selection process is equitable or transparent.

categories.label: Sanitation & Environmental Quality
categories.description: Comments about illegal dumping, waste cleanup, creek maintenance, air quality, and environmental health in public spaces. The main ask is cleanup, enforcement, or prevention related to waste and environmental conditions in public areas.
include: Illegal dumping on public land or near waterways
Coyote Creek and park cleanup
Free bulky-item pickup and dump-day programs
Air quality, noise, and environmental health near freeways or industrial areas
RV program conditions related to waste or environmental compliance
exclude: Habitability inside rental units → code_enforcement_habitability
Flood infrastructure (storm drains) → infrastructure_streets
Flood risk from development projects → environment_development_review
examples: There is a huge pile of mattresses and construction debris dumped along the Coyote Creek trail near Kelley Park. Been there weeks. I worry about it getting into the creek.
People dump because legal disposal is expensive and far. I SUPPORT more free bulky-item pickup and dump days.
The air near my place by 101 is visibly hazy and my kid's asthma is worse. I SUPPORT a sound/air wall and more trees along the corridor.

subcategories.label: Illegal Dumping & Creek Pollution
subcategories.description: Comments reporting mattresses, construction debris, or other waste dumped along Coyote Creek or public trails, and requesting cleanup.

subcategories.label: Dumping Prevention & Free Disposal Access
subcategories.description: Comments supporting free bulky-item pickup, dump days, and surveillance cameras at known hotspots as prevention-first alternatives to repeat cleanup.

subcategories.label: Freeway Air Quality & Noise
subcategories.description: Comments about hazy air, asthma, and noise near freeways, requesting sound or air walls and tree planting along high-traffic corridors.

categories.label: Other / General
categories.description: Catch-all for hardship stories with no specific agenda item ask, one-off topics, cover notes forwarding attachments, and messages too vague to place in another category.
include: Personal financial hardship (job loss, medical debt) seeking city help with no agenda item
Cover notes forwarding an attached letter with no independent content
Senior center service levels not tied to a specific agenda item
Comments expressing general frustration with cost of living without a specific policy ask
exclude: Any comment with a clear policy ask → assign to the relevant category above
examples: i dont know who to write to. i got laid off from a warehouse near monterey rd in april and cant find anything steady. im behind on rent and scared. is there any emergency help the city has??
Hello, Thank you for reviewing and responding to our attached comments. We look forward to continued discussion.
everything is too expensive here and nobody in charge seems to care. rent food gas all of it. i dont even know what im asking for anymore.

subcategories.label: Personal Financial Hardship
subcategories.description: Messages from residents describing job loss, medical debt, or inability to afford rent, with no specific agenda item or policy ask.

subcategories.label: Cover Note / Forwarded Attachment
subcategories.description: Emails whose entire content is a brief note forwarding an attached letter, with no independent substantive comment.

subcategories.label: General Cost-of-Living Frustration
subcategories.description: Comments expressing broad frustration about the cost of rent, food, and gas without articulating a specific policy ask.

subcategories.label: Senior Services (General)
subcategories.description: Comments about senior center hours, meal programs, or isolation that are not tied to a specific agenda item before the council.
